name: Sparrow Micro-VTOL
description: A two-seat vertical takeoff air taxi operating in Tier 3-5 airspace. Smaller and cheaper than a SkyLux, the Sparrow is the aerial equivalent of the AutoCab — hailable via app, fully autonomous, surveillance-equipped. It lands on designated pads atop buildings and whisks passengers across the city in minutes rather than hours. The ride is smooth and the view is worth the price if you can stomach the height.
propulsion: Eight-rotor electric VTOL with anti-grav assist
common_usage: Corporate commuting, time-sensitive transport, avoiding surface traffic entirely.
story_hooks: A Sparrow's AI diverts mid-flight and lands on an unregistered rooftop — the passenger finds themselves in a meeting they didn't request
Someone hacks the Sparrow fleet and every air taxi in the city lands simultaneously, paralyzing Tier 4-5 transit
physical_description: The Sparrow is a compact, angular aircraft with a weather-beaten composite fuselage painted matte gunmetal grey, its surface cratered by years of acid rain and UV exposure. Twin ducted rotors mounted on articulated arms fold against the narrow cabin—barely wide enough for two cramped seats—while exposed hydraulic lines and patched paneling hint at constant maintenance. A cracked polycarbonate canopy dominates the nose, and faded Tessera Transit decals peel from the tail boom.
